trivia_fact: NGINX was written by Igor Sysoev starting in 2002 to solve the C10K problem — the challenge of handling 10,000+ concurrent connections on a single server. Apache's process-per-connection model couldn't scale, so Sysoev designed an event-driven, asynchronous architecture.

NGINX is pronounced "engine-X," not "N-G-I-N-X." The name is sometimes written as "engine x" and the official stylization is all-caps NGINX. Many developers mispronounce it for years before learning the correct pronunciation.

NGINX was originally developed for Rambler, one of Russia's largest internet portals and search engines. Sysoev built it to handle Rambler's growing traffic. It was open-sourced in 2004, and by 2008 it was powering some of the world's busiest websites.

NGINX's event-driven, non-blocking architecture was revolutionary compared to Apache's process-per-connection model. A single NGINX worker process can handle thousands of concurrent connections using epoll (Linux) or kqueue (BSD), using a fraction of the memory Apache required.

F5 Networks acquired NGINX Inc. in March 2019 for $670 million. This was one of the largest acquisitions of an open-source company at the time. The acquisition gave F5 a modern software-based counterpart to its traditional hardware load balancers.

NGINX's configuration syntax was designed to be simpler than Apache's httpd.conf. It uses a C-like block structure with directives and contexts (http, server, location). The hierarchical design allows configuration inheritance, reducing repetition compared to Apache's per-directory model.

Although NGINX was created as a web server, it became most widely adopted as a reverse proxy and load balancer. By the mid-2010s, a common architecture pattern was NGINX in front of application servers (Node.js, Python, Ruby), handling SSL termination, caching, and load balancing.

NGINX overtook Apache as the most-used web server for the top million busiest websites around 2019. Apache had dominated since 1996, making NGINX's rise one of the most significant shifts in web infrastructure history.

In December 2019, Russian police raided NGINX's Moscow office and briefly detained Igor Sysoev. His former employer Rambler claimed ownership of NGINX's code, alleging it was developed on company time. The case was eventually dropped, but it highlighted open-source IP risks.

OpenResty, created by Yichun Zhang, embeds a LuaJIT interpreter into NGINX, allowing developers to write high-performance web applications directly inside NGINX. This turned NGINX from a web server into a full application platform, used at scale by Cloudflare and Kong.
